implementation_notes: lasso caches strings in an arena and hands back a Copy Spur key with O(1) intern and resolve; ThreadedRodeo is the concurrent interner, and once interning is finished it can be converted into RodeoReader or RodeoResolver for contention-free, read-only lookups at lower memory cost. The key is the flyweight handle, the arena entry is the intrinsic state, and extrinsic state lives in the struct holding the key. Choose it for string-heavy symbol tables and compiler-style workloads where keys are cheap to copy and the interner can be dropped as a unit.
pitfalls: Rodeo is not Sync: concurrent interning requires ThreadedRodeo (contended inserts) or an external lock, and the keys are only meaningful while the arena that produced them is alive.
The arena never frees individual entries: allocating one per request keeps every string until the interner is dropped, so long-lived interners need bounded key sets.
Resolving a key from a different interner of the same type is a logic error lasso cannot catch - keys are indices into their own arena.

variants.name: internment globally unique ArcIntern handles
variants.implementation_notes: internment interns arbitrary values rather than only strings and returns an ArcIntern<T> that is a single pointer-sized handle; equal values yield the same pointer, so equality and hashing degenerate to pointer comparison, and the entry is freed when the last handle is dropped. Intern<T> is the leak-forever variant, which is Copy and has no refcount traffic, and ArenaIntern ties lifetimes to an arena. Choose this variant when the intrinsic state is a struct (not a string) or when the pool must shrink again; pay for it with an atomic increment per clone.
pitfalls: Every clone and drop of ArcIntern performs an atomic operation, so a handle copied through a hot loop can cost more than the sharing saves.
Intern<T> never frees its values and is documented as such: choosing it for unbounded keys is a deliberate leak, not a cache.
Interned values must not be mutated through the handle: internment guarantees one shared representation, and interior mutability would make every holder observe the write.
